content.title: Service Line Inventory & Replacement Program
content.summary: The City of Arvada is collaborating with contractor Apex to identify and replace lead and pre-1960 galvanized customer-owned service lines, which are prohibited in the water system. As of early 2025, most service lines found are copper, with no lead lines detected, and the replacement program will cover affected properties at no cost until 2026. Homeowners are encouraged to report their service line materials, especially if their homes were built before 1960, to ensure compliance and safety.
content.body:
## Program overview

The City is working with our contractor, Apex (see logo) to locate and replace any remaining lead, or pre-1960 galvanized, customer-owned (private side) service lines. Lead and pre-1960 galvanized services lines are **prohibited**in Arvada's water system. These **lines should be replaced as soon as possible.**

Customers with lead lines, and lines that are uncategorized, may be issued fines beginning in 2027.

## What's happening now

### Service line inventory

As of early 2025, **we have found primarily copper service lines, a few galvanized lines and zero lead lines.**

The City continues to request information from our customers on their unknown service line materials ([see map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=960927ac3a7a4dccb104c3440fea172a)). The City’s hired contractor can schedule free visual inspections, potholing investigations, or replacements (for confirmed lead lines). Please complete this [form to request an inspection](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/47784) of your service line material.

[Inspection Request Form](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/47784)

Contact Arvada Water Quality for more information.

### Replacement Program

The replacement program for affected properties is effective as of May 1, 2024. Please continue reading the information below to determine the status of your property. **If your property is affected, the City will help replace your service line at no cost to you through 2026.**Please visit the [Service Line Replacement Program Details page for more information](/1025).

## What is a Water Service Line?

![service line connection to water main showing customer and system owned portions of a water line](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4697)A water service line is the connection from the drinking water main to the foundation of the home (or building). Each home's service line consists of two portions: the City owns the portion of the line from the drinking water main to the meter pit ("system-owned"), and the homeowner owns the portion of the line from the meter pit to their home's foundation ("customer-owned"). To check your service line material, you would find the location where the service line enters your home, usually in a basement or crawlspace.

### What you should know

1. **Was your home  built before 1960?**If so, and you think you may have a lead service line, contact us as soon as possible to be replaced.
2. **Does your home have galvanized lines?**Galvanized steel was used until the 1980s and can transmit small amounts of lead materials. If your home is pre-1960, and has a galvanized line, contact us as soon as possible to be replaced.
3. **What about internal (premise) plumbing?**The replacement program does not cover premise plumbing, however if you have galvanized or lead material, you should still plan on replacing it as you are able.
4. **What if the plumbing in your house has been replaced?**The service line may still contain lead materials. Let us know the materials so we can help determine if it should be replaced.
5. **Review the**[**service line inventory map**](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=960927ac3a7a4dccb104c3440fea172a). This map will be updated periodically with any new information. Please notify Arvada Water Quality of any discrepancies observed.

If your home was built before 1960 and you know or suspect you have a galvanized or lead water service line, or you are unsure what it is, please let us know! [**Complete this online survey**](https://arcg.is/0inWG80), [email Water Quality](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#39757a6b79584b4f585d5817564b5e), or call 720-898-7800.

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=49)

[How do I know what my portion of the service line is made of?](#)
:   Homes built after 1950 are more likely to have copper service lines.

    First, search for your address on the [City's service line inventory map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=960927ac3a7a4dccb104c3440fea172a). If your address is marked as unknown, follow the steps below to identify your service line material.

    You can often identify the material used in your service line through a visual inspection at the point where the water service line enters your home. Find where the water line enters your home and inspect the pipe. If you can access the pipe but you aren't sure what it is, perform a**"scratch test"** using a key or coin and test it for **magnetism**.

    You can scrape a small section with a coin if it is dirty or discolored.

    - If the scraped area is shiny and silver, your service line is lead. Lead is not magnetic.
    - If the scraped area is copper in color, like a penny, your service line is copper. Copper is not magnetic.
    - If the scraped area remains a dull gray, your service line is galvanized steel. Galvanized steel is magnetic.
    - The plumbing material may be PEX / plastic. In this case, it would appear to be plastic, not metal.

    Need help or still not sure? Take a picture of the service line and [email it along with the service address](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#4e020d1c0e2f3c382f2a2f60213c29) and a City team member will get back to you.

[What if I don’t want to replace my line (or my landlord doesn’t want to replace it)?](#)
:   Lead and pre-1960 galvanized services lines are **prohibited**in Arvada's water system. These **lines should be replaced as soon as possible.**

    If your property is impacted, the City will help replace your service line for free through 2026. Please visit the [Service Line Replacement Program Details page for more information](/1025). Customers with lead lines, and lines that are uncategorized, may be issued fines beginning in 2027.

    - If a lead service line is confirmed to be present, a certified lead-removing filter should be used for drinking water, cooking, and dishes where water is a base ingredient or absorbed into the food (recipes like rice, beans and soup) and preparing infant formula, until the line is replaced.

[I can’t afford to replace all my plumbing materials, what should I do?](#)
:   The City has implemented a free service line replacement program for impacted properties is effective May 1, 2024 through December 31, 2026. If your property is impacted, the City will help replace your service line (not premise plumbing) for free through 2026. Please visit the [Service Line Replacement Program page for more information](/647).

[What if my internal premise plumbing is galvanized too?](#)
:   If a copper pipe is connected to a galvanized line, a dielectric junction must be installed to reduce the potential for corrosion. It is recommended that internal galvanized lines be updated as well. The City's program is not replacing internal premise plumbing, this would be at the cost of the property owner.

[I have a lead or galvanized line, should I be worried for my family’s health?](#)
:   - Your health care provider is your best source of information and support for your family's health.
    - Visit the [Lead in Water Quality page](/841) for additional information and resources.

[Are there lead pipes in the system-owned portion of the water system?](#)
:   No. The City long ago removed all lead pipes from the system-owned portion of the water system.

[What are other ways I can reduce my family’s exposure to lead?](#)
:   - Replace old plumbing materials and fixtures, particularly lead, galvanized, or brass.
    - Run your cold tap for several seconds before use, and always use the cold side for consumption. You can warm water for cooking or formula on the stove or in the microwave.
    - The Colorado Department of Public Health and the Environment has made resources available on its website for residents to learn more about lead exposure. They have a [helpful brochure](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AfyfxtiHQWy7t9kxDIShj0iRAdb1mDnz/view) about common lead sources and health concerns.
    - The [EPA has resources available as well](https://www.epa.gov/lead).

[View All](/Faq.aspx?TID=49)

/FAQ.aspx
